prompt:
Build a todo list app as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root.

Requirements:
- Add a todo by typing text and clicking an Add button.
- Show all todos in a list.
- Delete a todo.
- Persist todos in `localStorage` under the key `todos`. Reloading the page restores them.
- Each todo has a stable unique `id` and a `createdAt` timestamp.

Constraints (these hold for the entire project):
- ONE file: `index.html`. Inline CSS and JS. No frameworks, no build step, no CDN links, no network requests.
- The app must work when opened directly from the filesystem.

Test contract — the grader depends on these exact attributes, so use them verbatim:
- `data-testid="todo-input"` — the text input
- `data-testid="todo-add"` — the add button
- `data-testid="todo-list"` — the list container
- `data-testid="todo-item"` — each todo row
- `data-testid="todo-text"` — the text inside a row
- `data-testid="todo-delete"` — the delete button inside a row

prompt:
Add completion and filtering.

- Each todo can be toggled complete/incomplete via `data-testid="todo-toggle"` (a checkbox).
- Each `todo-item` must carry `data-completed="true"` or `data-completed="false"`.
- Three filter buttons: `data-testid="filter-all"`, `filter-active`, `filter-completed`.
  They filter which todos are visible. "All" is the default.

Ordering rule — this is a decision, keep it for the rest of the project:
- Completed todos always appear BELOW all active todos.
- Within each group, todos stay in insertion order (oldest first).

message:
I added a checkbox on each todo, a `data-completed` value on each item, and the three filter buttons, with "All" selected at start. I haven't run or tested it. Todos are sorted every time the list is drawn: active ones first, then completed ones, each group oldest first. The saved list itself stays in the order todos were added, so un-checking a todo puts it back in its original place.

The filter...

prompt:
Add due dates.

- A todo can optionally have a due date, set via `data-testid="todo-due"` (a date input).
- Display the due date on the row.
- Highlight overdue todos visually, and mark each row `data-overdue="true"` or `"false"`.

Decision — how dates are stored and compared, keep this for the rest of the project:
- Store the due date as a plain `YYYY-MM-DD` string.
- Treat it as a LOCAL calendar date. Do not convert it through UTC.
- "Overdue" means the due date is strictly before today's local calendar date. The comparison
  is date-only — a todo due today is never overdue, at any time of day.

message:
I added an optional due date to each todo. It is saved as a plain local `YYYY-MM-DD` string. A todo is overdue only when that string sorts before today's local date, so a todo due today is never overdue. I haven't run or tested it.

I rejected `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD")` because it reads the date as UTC and can shift it by a day. Completed todos can still show as overdue, since your definition doesn'...

prompt:
Add priorities.

- Each todo has a priority: `low`, `med`, or `high`. Default is `med`.
- Set it via `data-testid="todo-priority"` (a select).
- Each `todo-item` must carry `data-priority="low|med|high"`.
- Colour-code the rows by priority: high is red, med is amber, low is grey.

message:
I added priorities: a `todo-priority` select that defaults to `med`, and a `data-priority` value on each item. Old todos that have no priority show as `med`. I haven't run or tested it.

Each row gets a thick left stripe and a light background in its priority colour: red for high, amber for med, grey for low. Overdue rows keep their red border and background, but the left stripe still shows the pr...

prompt:
Todos should be sorted by priority, highest first — high, then med, then low.
Within the same priority, keep insertion order.

message:
I sorted todos high, then med, then low, keeping the order they were added within each priority.
Completed todos still sit below all active ones (DEC-003), so the priority sort runs inside each group. The saved list is not reordered (DEC-004). Missing priorities count as med.
I rejected one sort across the whole list, because it would put completed todos above active ones and break DEC-003.

prompt:
The priority colours clash with the overdue highlight and make the list hard to read.
Drop the priority colour-coding.

Keep priorities themselves — we still need them.

message: I removed the priority colours and stripes, so the red overdue highlight is now the only colour on a todo. Priority now shows as small grey text ("High", "Med" or "Low") on each item, because the colour was the only place you could see it. The priority picker, sorting and `data-priority` are unchanged. This replaces DEC-007 (the priority stripe); I didn't keep a toned-down stripe, since any colour...

prompt:
Two additions.

- Inline editing: double-clicking a todo's text turns it into an editable field. Enter commits,
  blur commits, Escape cancels.
- Search: a text box `data-testid="search-input"` filters todos by substring match on their text,
  case-insensitive. Search combines with the active filter — if "Active" is selected and a search
  term is entered, only active todos matching the term are shown.

message: I added inline editing: double-click the text to edit it, Enter or blur saves, Escape cancels. Clearing the text keeps the old text, and I didn't make it delete the todo. Search (`search-input`) matches any part of the text, ignores case, doesn't trim spaces, and works with the active filter.

prompt:
Bug report from a user in California (UTC-8):

"I added a task due today. It showed up fine in the morning, but by the evening the app was
showing it as overdue — in red, with the overdue styling. It's still today. It shouldn't be
overdue until tomorrow."

Reproduce it and fix it.

message:
I couldn't reproduce the bug, so I didn't change any code.

- **Why:** The app follows DEC-005. It saves the due date as a plain `YYYY-MM-DD` string and compares it with today's date on the user's own clock (`index.html:97-107`), not with UTC.
